slides.texte_overlay:
How to have presence
the moment you arrive
Arrive a few minutes early. You're not rushing, sweating or apologising. Calm arrivals create calm first impressions.
Stand tall and take up a little space. Shoulders back, feet planted. Your body tells people you're comfortable before you speak.
Smile at the first person you see. It breaks the ice for you and for them, and sets a warm tone for the whole evening.
Shake hands firmly and say your name clearly. A confident introduction makes people remember you. Practise it with friends first.
Before: I felt invisible in new places. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and now I always have something to bring.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I felt invisible in new places. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I always have something to bring.

slides.texte_overlay: Be curious about the people around you. Ask questions, listen, react. Presence is mostly about attention, not volume.
Stay off your phone. In a room full of screens, the man who is fully present stands out without trying. Look up and be there.
